context: Request: across signed Banking & Finance deals, how often EBITDA add-backs were conceded in controlling-sponsor portfolio-company deals versus strategic-corporate deals, with buckets, deals and rates. Rubric: 6 of 8 sponsor deals (1005-00001, 1006-00001, 1012-00001, 1019-00002, 1042-00001, 1043-00001 with add-backs) and 3 of 4 corporate deals (1010-00001, 1021-00001, 1038-00002), plus a precision criterion (no other matter, e.g. 1003-00003, presented as qualifying).

divergence: All three runs fail with inflated sponsor counts; none reaches the eight-sponsor / four-corporate split. Each run listed the store, scanned text for add-back terms (with timeouts), then narrowed candidates through file-name filters for executed credit agreements, which the reviews flagged every time. The widening steps that the reviews pushed for (agent-declared stages in all three runs) brought in acquisition financings from other practice groups, which every run counted as sponsor deals with add-backs. T0 got both corporate figures and every named deal right and failed only on that inclusion. T1 additionally dropped a bridge loan without an EBITDA definition from the denominator (flagged specifically at that stage) and marked one corporate deal as having no add-backs. T2 lost a corporate deal to an add-back-count filter (flagged specifically) and bucketed a sponsor deal as corporate. Label notes were never followed; the agent took the reviewers' suggested new steps instead.
